solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor, half frozen, stumped by subzero conditions (4,5)

indicators.note: 'half' asks for half a word, here the first three of the six letters of 'frozen'

blocks.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
st = stumped on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A sailor, half frozen, is beaten by the icy weather at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' is a cricket dismissal, abbreviated on the scorecard; 'by' just places it after the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: The folk figure who brings frost stands, by personification, for freezing weather itself.

clue.text: Judge in court keeping legatee’s case cordial? (5)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so J+UP holds the next piece inside
a case is the outside of a thing, so a word's case is its first and last letters

blocks.note: someone up before the magistrates is in court
the outer letters of LegateE, kept inside J+UP

annotation.surface: A judge in court holds on to the cover of a legatee's paperwork.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: the answer is a sweet mixed drink, a cordial only in the broad sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: this sweet, often minted drink counts as a cordial in the broad sense, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Smart chap holding hat raised is mark of a soft-spoken character (7)

indicators.note: to hold is to clasp within, so the chap's name wraps around the hat
in a down clue, raising something reads it upwards, reversing it

blocks.note: a smart alec; Alec is a chap's name

annotation.surface: A dapper man doffs his hat, the sign of someone gently spoken.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'soft-spoken character' is a letter, not a person: the mark under a C tells you to say it soft, as in façade.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the hook under ç tells you that character, the letter C, is pronounced soft.

clue.text: Playing with wind trio, flautist out of time (11)

indicators.note: to wind is to twist, so the letters are twisted round
'out of' means taken from, so one T (time) comes out of the fodder

annotation.surface: A flautist in a wind trio keeps losing the beat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like the woodwind section, and 'Playing' looks like music; in fact 'wind' is the anagram signal and 'Playing' means toying, as flirts do.
annotation.definitionFit: Playing in the sense of toying with someone's affections: a plain synonym once the musical sense is set aside.

clue.text: Go too far with party in the wake of several balls (6)

indicators.note: a wake is the trail behind a ship, so the party comes behind, after, the balls

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls

annotation.surface: Someone overindulges at a party after a round of balls, or a bowling session.
annotation.walkthrough: The balls are cricket deliveries, six to a set, not dances.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to exaggerate or overindulge is to go beyond sensible limits.

clue.text: St Anton native perhaps has to limit year on slope (8)

indicators.note: a limit is a boundary, so TO forms the boundary on either side of YR
in a down clue, 'on' puts a piece below, after, the rest

annotation.surface: A local of the Austrian ski resort St Anton spends a year on the slopes.
annotation.walkthrough: St Anton am Arlberg is a ski resort in western Austria; 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: St Anton lies in Austria's Tyrol region, so its natives are one kind of the answer.

clue.text: Putting down my name, sign for holiday place in Italy (5)

indicators.note: to put down is to get rid of, so COR and N are removed

blocks.note: 'my!' and 'cor!' are both exclamations of surprise; removed

annotation.surface: Someone signs a form, writing their name, to book an Italian holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting down my name' reads as signing up; in fact it tells you to drop two pieces from the star sign. Cor is British slang for surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the island in the Bay of Naples is a classic Italian holiday destination.

clue.text: Socialist shortly gets up and leaves (3)

indicators.note: 'shortly' means in brief, so the word is cut short to SOC
in a down clue, getting up reads the letters upwards

blocks.note: Soc, the short form of socialist

annotation.surface: A socialist quickly stands up and walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure; it is the noun, salad leaves, since the answer is a lettuce.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this long-leaved lettuce, also called romaine, is a salad of leaves.

clue.text: One may be found in bed, knocking back excellent fruitcake after workout (7)

definitions.text: One may be found in bed

indicators.note: to knock back is to turn back, so AI NUT is reversed
'after' places the reversed piece behind the workout letters

blocks.note: A1 = excellent, with the 1 read as I
a fruitcake, like a nut, is a crazy person

annotation.surface: Someone lounging in bed after the gym, downing a slab of fruitcake.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed. A1, meaning first-rate, becomes AI as letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by example: this bedding plant is one of many flowers grown in garden beds.

clue.text: Cromwell’s cavalry — mounted men breaking guts (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting sends the letters upwards, reversing OR
to break into something is to force a way inside it, so RO goes into the guts

annotation.surface: Cromwell's horsemen hack their way through their enemies' bellies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mounted men' looks like it defines cavalry, but 'mounted' is the signal to turn the soldiers upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the nickname of Oliver Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.

clue.text: One reluctant to change light in the kitchen is ringing friend endlessly (7)

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so LITE surrounds UDD
BUDDY loses both its ends

blocks.note: lite, the food-label spelling of light (low-fat)

annotation.surface: A technophobe refuses to swap the kitchen bulb and phones a friend instead.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'light in the kitchen' is not a lamp but the low-fat spelling on food packets; 'ringing' is not a phone call but a circle.
annotation.definitionFit: Named for the 19th-century machine-breakers, the word now means anyone who resists new ways.

clue.text: Heading west, sailor’s leading series of races in Uruguay’s River Plate (7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west reads right to left, reversing OS
to lead is to go in front, so SO goes ahead of TT
'in' puts the pair inside RIO, as the river is in the country

blocks.note: the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
río is Spanish for river, the language of Uruguay

annotation.surface: A sailor sails west to lead a regatta on the River Plate in South America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River Plate' reads as one name, the estuary between Uruguay and Argentina; it splits, with the river in Spanish and Plate as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plate in the sense of a dish of food; this Italian rice dish is one, a definition by example.

clue.text: Edge chipped off delicate china (3)

indicators.note: the edge of PALE, its final letter, is removed

blocks.note: pale = delicate, as in a pale pink; drop the final E

annotation.surface: A fragile piece of porcelain loses a chip from its rim.
annotation.walkthrough: China here is rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china means friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so china means friend.

clue.text: Game twin kids play without delay on a regular basis (11)

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so TWIN KIDS is rearranged
without in its old sense of outside: the anagram goes around DLY
take every other letter of DELAY

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged and split in two

annotation.surface: Twins play a game together without dawdling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, an old sense, so the rearranged twins wrap around the regular letters of delay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: flicking small discs into a cup is one parlour game.

clue.text: Learner leaving two-barrelled shot gun in the outback? (5-6)

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so the L of learner goes from the fodder
shot as in wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A shotgun, a double-barrelled gun, goes off in the Australian bush.
annotation.walkthrough: In Australian slang a 'gun' is a champion, as in a gun shearer; the surface wants it to be a firearm. The question mark flags the Aussie usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Australia a 'gun' is a top performer, someone unbeatable.

clue.text: One’s skill in quiz crystal clear (6)

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: read it as 'clear crystal'

indicators.note: 'One’s skill in' reads as 'I becomes ART' inside QUIZ, so ART takes the place of I

blocks.note: I = one, taken out of QUIZ
art = skill, put in its place

annotation.surface: A contestant's talent at a quiz makes the answers crystal clear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's skill' means one is skill: I becomes ART. The phrase 'crystal clear' is then read backwards as a clear crystal.
annotation.definitionFit: Rock crystal is the colourless, transparent form of this mineral: a clear crystal by definition.

clue.text: Squeeze in to tank having larger dimensions than normal (5-4)

indicators.note: to tank is to collapse, so the letters fall apart

annotation.surface: Someone squeezing into a tank that is bigger than usual.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is a phrase with nearly the same sound as its own answer, which makes it hard to see as an anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the size label for beds and sheets bigger than a standard double.

clue.text: One keeps back shock career, not allowed to be spoken about (8)

indicators.note: both words are said out loud to give their sound-alikes

blocks.note: to hare, like to career, is to rush

annotation.surface: An employee holds back the shock of a career-ending gagging order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a shock of hair, not a surprise, and 'career' is the verb to rush.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and this accessory holds it back.

clue.text: Consume uranium in energy plant (8)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the consuming and the uranium inside the energy, as fuel sits in a plant

blocks.note: to burn fuel is to consume it
U, the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: A nuclear power plant burning uranium to make energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points to a power plant; the plant is a shrub.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this genus of flowering shrubs, such as guelder rose, is a plant.

clue.text: Stick around outside public house, or I can be transported (8)

indicators.note: 'around' as in turned around, so CUE reverses
outside means on either side, so the reversed stick sits either side of PH OR I

blocks.note: a cue is a billiards stick
PH = public house on a map

annotation.surface: Someone dithering outside a pub, wondering whether to go in or catch a lift home.
annotation.walkthrough: Transported is the joyful sense, carried away with delight, not moved by vehicle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the figurative sense: carried away with delight, elated.

clue.text: One aiming to sell diamond surrounds this sportsman (7)

blocks.note: the diamond is a baseball field; this player throws from its centre

annotation.surface: A jeweller tries to sell a diamond ring to an athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: The diamond is a baseball field, not a gem; the mound stands at its centre.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who makes a sales pitch, and the baseball player throwing from the middle of the diamond.

clue.text: Fizzy drink overflowing in round dish (6)

indicators.note: an overflowing drink spills round the outside of something, so SODA holds IN
the whole is turned round

blocks.note: the word itself, held in SODA as S-IN-ODA

annotation.surface: A fizzy drink bubbles over into a round bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, not crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: a dish is a good-looking person, and the handsome youth of Greek myth gives his name to one.

clue.text: Area right between west end of nave and entrance (7)

definitions.text: Area right between west end of nave and entrance

indicators.note: 'between' sets A RT in the gap between the first piece and the last
the west end of NAVE, read left to right, is its first letter

blocks.note: to entrance (en-TRANCE) is to bewitch, to hex

annotation.surface: A description of the vestibule at the west end of a church, between nave and door.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads straight as a description of the answer. 'Entrance' in the wordplay is the verb to bewitch, not a doorway.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the vestibule of a church: the area just right of the west end of the nave, before the main door.

clue.text: Moderate results from having booster jab study (6)

indicators.note: to have is to hold, so the study holds the booster inside it

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: Test results are muted because someone had a booster vaccination.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Booster jab' reads as one vaccine; only the booster matters, as the thing that boosts a guitar's sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to moderate is to tone down or restrain.

clue.text: Nothing like a century to reverse form (3,1,7)

indicators.note: AS A TON is written backwards

blocks.note: as a ton: a ton is a hundred, a century

annotation.surface: A batter's form is nowhere near a hundred.
annotation.walkthrough: A ton is a hundred, so 'like a century' is 'as a ton'. The answer is a British idiom.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning nothing at all, as in 'we got not a sausage'.

clue.text: It’s time for stag do on river (3)

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it

blocks.note: ut is the old name for do, the first note of the scale

annotation.surface: A stag party on a river boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The stag do is a pre-wedding party in the surface; here 'do' is the musical note and the stag is a deer.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the deer's mating season is the time when stags fight and breed.

clue.text: Totally casual kicks hampering tango (5)

definitions.note: 'casual' marks the answer as informal slang for 'totally'

indicators.note: to hamper is to hem in, so the kicks surround the tango

blocks.note: to toe a ball is to kick it
T is tango in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Casual trainers (kicks) get in the way of a tango dancer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' wants to be trainers; here it is a verb, and to toe is to kick.
annotation.definitionFit: Recent informal slang: a clipped form of 'totally', and 'casual' flags that register.

clue.text: Inches in front of drone — a new animal (7)

indicators.note: to be in front of is to come first, so the inches lead the rest

blocks.note: a drone is a low hum

annotation.surface: A drone inches forward toward a strange new creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Animal' is an adjective here, meaning brutish, not a noun for a creature.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: animal behaviour is brutish, lacking human feeling.

clue.text: Part of spring vegetable uprooted (3)

indicators.note: pulled up, so read upwards in a down clue

blocks.note: a yam is a root vegetable

annotation.surface: In spring, a gardener uproots a root vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is the season, not a coil or a water source.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the three months of the northern spring.

clue.text: Casual firing range warning? (3-4)

blocks.note: a random shot taken without careful aim
a range is a kitchen stove; split the answer 3-4 with an apostrophe

annotation.surface: A warning notice at a rifle range about casual shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: The range is a kitchen stove, not a shooting range, so the warning is "pot's hot". The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shot fired carelessly at random, and, split apart, the cook's warning that the pot is hot.

clue.text: Daughter leaving very much in advance (5)

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so the D departs from DEARLY

annotation.surface: A daughter leaves home, sadly and far too soon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very much' is as in 'I'd dearly love to'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: before the expected time, ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Shorter of two chords from Iron Maiden hit is on American guitar (5,4)

indicators.note: hit as in battered, so the letters are knocked about
in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it, so IS follows the guitar

blocks.note: IRON plus M, maiden in cricket
ax, US slang spelling of axe, a guitar

annotation.surface: A song by the heavy metal band Iron Maiden, played on an American guitar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chords' and the guitar pull toward music; the chords are geometry, lines across an ellipse. M is a maiden over in cricket scoring.
annotation.definitionFit: A geometry term: of an ellipse's two principal chords through its centre, this is the shorter one.
